newsitem.title: USA: Excel CFO sees 1998 EPS at $1.80-$2.20.
newsitem.headline: Excel CFO sees 1998 EPS at $1.80-$2.20.

text.p: Excel Communications Inc Chief Financial Officer Jack McLaine said the company's proposed acquisition of Telco Communications Group Inc would push its 1998 earnings per share up to between $1.80 and $2.20.
"We are now estimating earnings per share will be in the range of $1.80 to $2.20," McLaine told Reuters after the $1.2 billion merger deal was announced.
He said most analysts had expected Excel, standing alone, to run up earnings per share of about $1.60 in 1998.
McLaine said Excel would win hefty cost savings by shifting its long-distance traffic onto Telco's network.

"It is basically going to reduce our transmission costs, our communication costs, by about 20 percent, between 1.5 cents and 2.0 cents per minute," McLaine said. "That's another benefit of this: there is no guess work."
Excel currently buys wholesale long-distance service from companies with networks and resells it to customers through its multilevel structure of independent sales reps.

McLaine said the process of shifting traffic away from Excel's wholesale suppliers and onto Telco's network would take about 18 months after the merger is expected to be completed at the end of this year.
"The savings will kick in in 1998 and 1999, and there will be even greater synergies in 1999 and 2000," he said.

He said Excel planned to invest about $20 million over the next two years in expanding the port capacity of the Telco switch network and said there may be additional investment in the purchase of additional fiber optic strands.
